rows.name: coin_count
rows.notes: HUD coin counter behind the "x" in the status bar. Found with no reference by differential search on the two ?-block coins in World 1-1: snapshot before/after the 1st coin and diff 'increased' gave 127 survivors, then a 2nd coin and diff 'increased' from the first narrowed it to 17, in which 0x07EE went 1 -> 2 (the ones digit) while 0x07ED stayed 0 matching the on-screen "x02". Encoding proven by write + forced full HUD redraw: wrote 0x07ED=3, 0x07EE=5, then set the timer to 001 and let the time-up death reload the level (the reload redraws the whole status bar) - the resulting screenshot showed the HUD coin display "x35", matching the two bytes and their order (tens then ones); the earlier live value 0x07ED=0 / 0x07EE=2 matched the displayed "x02". Note the differential search alone points at the ones byte 0x07EE; the write test is what fixes the tens byte 0x07ED and the order. Source: differential search.

rows.name: level_timer
rows.notes: The TIME counter. Found with no reference by differential search: an idle interval (no input) diffed 'decreased' left 19 survivors including 0x07F9; reading 0x07F8-0x07FA gave 3,3,0 while the screen read TIME 330, and later 2,6,6 while the screen read 266, i.e. one decimal digit per byte, hundreds first. Proven by write_memory: wrote 0x07FA=9 (screen read 266) and let the timer tick - RAM became 8 and the HUD showed TIME 268, i.e. the game decremented from my written digit and redrew the ones tile. Full extent proven the same way: wrote 0x07F7=1, 0x07F8=3, 0x07F9=0, 0x07FA=0, 0x07FB=2; after one tick the RAM was 0x07F7=1, 0x07F8=2, 0x07F9=9, 0x07FA=9 and the screenshot showed TIME 299 - the timer redrew all three digits from RAM and the values written to the neighbouring bytes 0x07F7/0x07FB never appeared. Source: differential search.

rows.name: score
rows.notes: MARIO's score. Found with no reference by differential search on two ?-block coins (each +200): diff 'increased' over the 1st coin kept 127 candidates, the 2nd coin narrowed it to 17, in which 0x07E1 went 2 -> 4 while the HUD score's hundreds digit went 2 -> 4 (200 -> 400). Reading 0x07DD-0x07E2 gave 0,0,0,0,4,0 while the status bar showed 000400. Extent and byte order proven by write + forced full HUD redraw: wrote 0x07DC=9, 0x07DD=1, 0x07DE=2, 0x07DF=3, 0x07E0=4, 0x07E1=0, 0x07E2=5, 0x07E3=6, 0x07E4=7, then set the timer to 001 and let the time-up death reload the level (the reload redraws the whole status bar); the screenshot showed the HUD score 1234050, i.e. exactly the six digits 0x07DD-0x07E2 in order followed by the fixed ones-place 0. The bytes written one past each end (0x07DC, 0x07E3, 0x07E4) never appeared on screen; 0x07DC was also cleared to 0 by the reload. Source: differential search.
